title: The snail and the station clock

data.source: One smooth path with back-steps, replayed under three stretchings of time (Phoenix study TWO-CLOCKS-MC-2026-10-06, checks 1a and 2a). The real-data scores are read from Phoenix_Egg/README.md and were not re-run.

prediction: As arithmetic: stretching time, or waiting, changes the seconds and leaves the count of change and the number of occasions alone. As a claim about the world (Phoenix's registered hypothesis): a predictor built on the clock of change beats predictors built on ordinary time and phase, on held-out real records.
baseline: For the arithmetic, the change-of-variable rule of calculus. For the world, the native phase, rate-state and clock models the registered predictor had to beat.
why: The arithmetic holds and could not do otherwise. The claim about the world was tested on real data three times and failed three times (0 of 17 cities, 1 of 29 and 5 of 29 heart records), none of them narrowly. Phoenix keeps the idea as a set of constructions, not as a supported hypothesis.
phoenix_status: "The two clocks failed as an empirical hypothesis." (H-L5: MEAS2-1 0/17, CARD-1 1/29, CARD-2 5/29, "none was fragile".) The formal checks: layer formal, rung none, 17 of 17 behave as the mathematics requires; "sound and modest"; a reduction to "time-change invariance plus renewal theory". The reading "local becoming with no global Now": NOT DECIDABLE (ND-3).
